title: Per-request provenance envelope and adaptive span enrichment for tiered-region routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Current routing observability captures per-hop metrics and decision records but lacks a compact, forward-compatible envelope that travels with each request across region/tier/fallback hops. This makes it hard to correlate transient policy decisions (tier downgrade, model fallback) with downstream quality regressions and cost spikes. Goal: introduce a lightweight per-request provenance envelope plus an adaptive span enrichment layer that attaches contextual breadcrumbs only when helpful (based on sampling, privacy, and cost budgets). The envelope must be size-bounded, privacy-aware (no plaintext PII), and easy to forward to the Console for debugging and SLO analysis. Scope: 1) define envelope wire-format and canonical fields (route_id, route_version, tier_affinity_score, fallback_variant_fingerprint, routing_policy_tags, hop_index, local_decision_reason_codes, hashed_customer_id, sampling_seed). 2) implement envelope propagation in the router and proxy layer for hosted & dedicated paths. 3) implement an adaptive span enrichment controller that decides per-request whether to attach extra context (inputs snapshot hashes, KV cache hits, kernel selection hints) and which level of enrichment to use: minimal, debug, forensic. 4) add conservative default sampling (0.5% forensic, 5% debug, 100% minimal) with per-customer overrides and emergency-on triggers when SLO/quality regressions are detected. 5) UI and query plumbing in Console: surface per-request provenance, allow replay of routing decisions, and expose aggregated metrics for tier downgrades and fallback frequency by region/model. Non-goals: full-request payload capture (we only keep hashed or truncated fingerprints), long-term retention of forensic envelopes (short TTL).
acceptance_criteria: Envelope schema RFC merged and published in Confluence
Router and proxy propagate envelope without >2% p50 latency regressions in synthetic benchmarks
Adaptive span enrichment honors privacy rules (no raw user PII stored) and sampling budgets
Console shows a per-request provenance panel and an aggregated metric card for fallback rates by region/model
Unit + integration tests for envelope encoding/decoding and sampling policy controller
Can opt-in per-customer forensic level via Dedicated/Private tenancy settings
notes: 2026-03-10: Kickoff meeting — agreed to use a compact binary base64 envelope with version tag to allow future fields. Trade-off: binary reduces wire size but needs explicit schema versioning; decided acceptable due to bandwidth concerns in high-throughput paths.

2026-03-11: Prototype: router attaches 'env' header with base64-encoded envelope. Initial fields: {route_id, hop_index, tier, fallback_variant, affinity_score, seed}. Marco measured +0.8ms p50 in router-only microbenchmarks (on dev cluster). Need further optimizations to meet target.
2026-03-11: SRE review: recommended capping envelope at 512 bytes; reject any attempt to attach raw inputs. Also suggested adding a flag to drop envelopes on constrained nodes to avoid OOM risk.
2026-03-12: PM feedback (Sofia Nguyen): include per-customer override and emergency sampling toggle tied to SLO alerts. Also requested a Console query to list recent rollback-triggered fallbacks.
2026-03-12: Security review requested — see links below. Marked security_review_required = true.

Implementation plan: 1) RFC and schema; 2) lightweight encoder lib (go/rs/python) used by router & runtime; 3) sampling controller service extension (policy engine); 4) Console ingestion + view; 5) staged rollout (internal-only -> opt-in customers -> default on with conservative sampling).

Trade-offs considered: - Full trace inclusion vs envelope only: envelope chosen to minimize perf cost. - Always-on debug traces vs adaptive sampling: adaptive chosen to keep costs predictable. - Binary vs JSON: binary chosen but we will provide JSON decoding helpers in tools/console for inspection.
